solution:
[Textbook answer-key error: the printed key \(x-1=y-1=z-2\) has direction \((1,1,1)\), which is NOT perpendicular to \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) (dot product \(=4\neq0\)); the correct direction is \(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\propto(1,-1,1)\), as derived below.]

The line is perpendicular to both \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), so its direction is \(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\).
\(\bar{b}\times\bar{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&1\\3&2&-1\end{vmatrix}=\hat{i}(2(-1)-1\cdot2)-\hat{j}(1\cdot(-1)-1\cdot3)+\hat{k}(1\cdot2-2\cdot3)\)
\(=-4\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\), proportional to \(1,-1,1\).
Using \(A(1,1,2)\):
\(\therefore \frac{x-1}{1}=\frac{y-1}{-1}=\frac{z-2}{1}\).

solution:
A plane making equal intercepts \(a\) on all three axes has intercept equation
\(\dfrac{x}{a}+\dfrac{y}{a}+\dfrac{z}{a}=1\ \Rightarrow\ x+y+z=a\)
It passes through \(A(1,2,3)\): \(1+2+3=a\Rightarrow a=6\).
It passes through \(B(3,2,1)\): \(3+2+1=a\Rightarrow a=6\).
Both points give the same value \(a=6\), so the plane is
\(x+y+z=6\)
The vector equation is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)=6\).
(Note: with the equal-intercept condition \(x+y+z=a\), both given points force \(a=6\), so there is a unique such plane.)

The stem asks for plane(s): besides the nonzero-intercept plane above, the degenerate case of equal (all-zero) intercepts is a plane through the origin. The plane through the origin containing \(A(1,2,3)\) and \(B(3,2,1)\) has normal \(\overline{OA}\times\overline{OB}=(1,2,3)\times(3,2,1)=(-4,8,-4)\propto(1,-2,1)\), giving
\(x-2y+z=0\), i.e. \(\bar{r}\cdot(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k})=0\)
(check: \(A: 1-4+3=0\), \(B: 3-4+1=0\)). So the two required planes are \(x+y+z=6\) and \(x-2y+z=0\).
